verdict.rationale: Ironclad documents issuing its own API credentials: you register an OAuth client application and use the Client Credentials Grant to generate bearer tokens, which an agent could use. Nothing in the evidence shows those credentials can be limited to specific resources or permissions, so the least-privilege core of the story is unproven. The API also requires a paid add-on. Missing for 10: documented OAuth scopes or per-client permission restrictions, any least-privilege or agent-specific credential guidance, token expiry/rotation details, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Ironclad primarily uses the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework to generate API bearer tokens that can be used to authenticate API requests.
